data.title: Harbor Diversified Delays Its Quarterly Report Filing
data.description:
Harbor BioSciences ( (HRBR) ) has released a notification of late filing.

Harbor Diversified, Inc. filed Form 12b-25 (Notification of Late Filing) for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The delayed report is its Form 10-Q (Quarter Report), which the company says it could not complete by the prescribed deadline without unreasonable effort or expense.

The company and its independent registered public accounting firm devoted considerable time and resources to financial statement preparation, audit and review work. That work covered the company’s Form 10-K (Yearly Report) for 2025 and several earlier Form 10-Q (Quarter Report) filings, while resources were also directed toward the sale and disposition of its aviation assets.

Harbor Diversified does not expect to file the Form 10-Q (Quarter Report) within the five-day extension available under the late-filing rule. The notification does not provide a specific new filing date, so investors have not been given a firm timeline for the delayed report.

The company anticipates significant changes in its financial condition and results of operations compared with historical periods. After the aviation disposition, it says it has no material operating assets, is not engaged in an operating business, and has no source of revenue from operations; no quantitative preliminary results were provided.

The filing also states that the Form 10-Q (Quarter Report) filings for the quarters ended March 31, 2026, and June 30, 2026, remained outstanding. Harbor Diversified cautions that statements about the expected filing timing are forward-looking and could differ because of risks and uncertainties; the notification was signed by Chief Executive Officer and Secretary Christine R. Deister on November 20, 2026.

data.title: Natural Grocers Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Costs
data.description:
Natural Grocers By Vitamin Cottage ((NGVC)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Natural Grocers delivered a broadly positive fiscal 2026 earnings call, supported by its 23rd consecutive year of positive comparable-store sales growth, record full-year diluted EPS, strong liquidity, store expansion, and encouraging e-commerce results. However, lower gross margin, higher shrink and freight costs, declining transactions, and new-store expenses tempered the performance and contributed to a fourth-quarter EPS decline.

23rd Year of Positive Comparable Sales

Natural Grocers marked its 23rd consecutive year of positive comparable-store sales growth in fiscal 2026. Daily average comparable sales accelerated in each of the final two quarters, reaching 2.5% in the fourth quarter.

Fourth-Quarter Sales Momentum

Fourth-quarter net sales rose 3.4% year over year to $347.5 million, while daily average comparable sales increased 2.5%. Comparable sales were up 6.7% on a two-year basis, helped by contributions from stores opened during fiscal 2026.

Record Full-Year Earnings

Fiscal 2026 diluted EPS increased 1.5% to $2.03 from $2.00, setting a company record. Adjusted EBITDA also edged higher, rising 0.5% to $98.4 million.

{N}power Membership Engagement

The {N}power loyalty program accounted for 85% of fourth-quarter sales, up from 82% a year earlier. Management said traffic and basket growth among highly engaged members supported personalized offers and helped reconnect with lapsed customers.

Differentiated Categories Lead Growth

Natural Grocers said its most differentiated categories continued to outperform overall sales growth. Meat, produce, and dairy remained important drivers as the company emphasized its assortment and natural-food positioning.

Store Expansion Accelerates

Fiscal 2026 was the first year of the company’s accelerated unit-growth strategy, with seven stores opened and entry into its 22nd state. Management said the development pipeline can support further expansion, with opportunities remaining in both existing and new markets.

E-Commerce Capabilities Expand

DoorDash delivery reached all stores with in-store pricing and integrated {N}power rewards, while website shopping tools were enhanced. Curbside pickup through Instacart also reached every location, and early results showed incremental transactions from existing customers and interest from new shoppers.

Natural Grocers Brand Gains Share

Natural Grocers brand products represented 9.3% of fourth-quarter sales, compared with 8.8% a year earlier. The company introduced 68 new private-label items during fiscal 2026, supporting product differentiation and customer value.

Expense Management Provides Benefits

Fourth-quarter store expenses as a percentage of sales fell 13 basis points, mainly because of expense management. For the full year, the ratio was 34 basis points lower than in fiscal 2025.

Liquidity and Free Cash Flow Remain Strong

Natural Grocers ended the quarter with $32.1 million in cash and no credit-facility borrowings, while $67.5 million remained available under its revolving facility. Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow was $87.4 million, net capital expenditures were $53.5 million, and free cash flow reached $33.9 million.

Value Proposition Supports Loyalty

Management reported no meaningful increase in competitive or promotional pressure from mass-market and conventional retailers. The Even More Affordable campaign was described as effective, with one $3.99 organic egg offering selling nearly 50% more units than a $2.99 conventional alternative.

New-Store Costs Viewed as Investment

New-store expenses reduced fourth-quarter and full-year results by approximately $0.02 and $0.09 per share, respectively. Management characterized those costs as investments intended to build future earnings capacity as the store base expands.

Fourth-Quarter Gross Margin Declines

Fourth-quarter gross margin fell 21 basis points to 29.2%, primarily because product margin was pressured by higher inventory shrink and freight costs. Better occupancy-cost leverage partially offset the decline.

Full-Year Margin Remains Under Pressure

Fiscal 2026 gross margin declined 31 basis points from the prior year, largely due to higher merchandise shrink. Management expects margin pressure from shrink and freight trends to continue into the first half of fiscal 2027.

Fourth-Quarter EPS Falls Below Outlook

Fourth-quarter net income declined to $11.3 million, and diluted EPS fell to $0.48 from $0.51 a year earlier. The result was below the company’s August outlook, mainly because lower gross margin and higher pre-opening costs outweighed sales growth.

Comparable Transactions Remain Negative

Daily average comparable transaction count decreased 0.5% in the fourth quarter. Still, the decline improved by 130 basis points from the previous quarter, suggesting some progress in customer traffic trends.

Items per Basket Decline

Customers purchased 0.2 fewer items per basket during the fourth quarter. The decline added to pressure on transaction productivity even as comparable sales remained positive.

Pre-Opening Expenses Increase

Fourth-quarter pre-opening expenses rose $500,000 year over year, while the full-year increase was $2 million. The higher costs reflected the faster pace of store openings and the associated preparation for new locations.

Shrink and Freight Create Operational Challenges

Management identified shrink as an ongoing operational issue, citing power outages, unusual product mix linked to the UNFI cyber incident, and ERP-related process changes. Freight affected results by roughly 15% to 20% in the quarter and approximately 15% for the full year, while inventory controls and store-accountability initiatives are being implemented.

New Stores Raise Depreciation and Amortization

The gap between adjusted EBITDA growth and lower fourth-quarter net income largely reflected higher depreciation from new-store investment and ERP-related amortization. These costs are expected to remain a factor as recent stores mature and additional locations are developed.

Store-Expense Deleverage Expected

Store expenses as a percentage of sales are expected to increase slightly in fiscal 2027. Management attributed the expected change primarily to deleverage from newer store vintages as those locations continue ramping toward maturity.

Tax Rate Reflects Colorado Change

Natural Grocers estimates a fiscal 2027 income tax rate of 22.5% to 23%. The forecast includes a preliminary effect from Colorado Amendment 87, which moves the state to a graduated income-tax structure beginning in 2027.

Fiscal 2027 Guidance and Investment Plan

Natural Grocers expects to open 7 to 9 stores, relocate or remodel 2 to 4 locations, and deliver daily average comparable sales growth of 2% to 3% in fiscal 2027. The company also expects diluted EPS of $2.03 to $2.10 and capital expenditures of $55 million to $60 million, with openings weighted toward the back half of the year.

Management expects comparable sales growth to improve modestly as the year progresses, with the first half closer to current levels and acceleration in the second half. E-commerce initiatives are expected to provide an additional lift, while full-year gross margin should be relatively flat, pre-opening expenses should total $3.5 million to $4 million, and new-store investments are expected to reduce EPS by about $0.12 year over year.

Natural Grocers enters fiscal 2027 with durable sales momentum, strong liquidity, and a larger growth pipeline, while operational pressures remain important risks. The call’s overall tone was constructive, but investors will likely watch shrink, freight, traffic, and the profitability ramp of new stores closely.

data.title: FINDEP Issues Additional US$10 Million of Senior Notes Due 2028
data.description:
An update from Financiera Independencia SAB de CV ( (MX:FINDEP) ) is now available.

Financiera Independencia issued an additional US$10 million of its 9.25% Senior Notes due May 20, 2028, bringing the principal amount to US$35 million. The notes pay interest semiannually and were issued under the company’s Euro Short-Term Note Program, established for up to US$100 million.

The company will use the net proceeds to grow its loan portfolio and for general corporate purposes. The notes are not registered with Mexico’s CNBV and may not be publicly offered or sold in Mexico; related offering documents were not submitted to or approved by regulatory authorities.

data.title: Sizzle Acquisition Corporation II Announces Annual Meeting and Shareholder Proposals
data.description:
An update from Sizzle Acquisition Corporation II Class A ( (SZZL) ) is now available.

Sizzle Acquisition Corp. II said it will hold its annual general meeting on Dec. 29, 2026, at 11 a.m. Eastern Time in New York, with shareholder proposals due by Nov. 30, 2026. The meeting is required under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5620(a) for the company’s first annual meeting for fiscal 2025.

At the meeting, the terms of the Class I directors will expire, while Class B shareholders will exclusively elect, remove or replace directors before a business combination; Class A shareholders have no voting rights on those matters. A written ordinary resolution on reappointing the Class I directors will be presented to Class B shareholders.

data.title: Energy Vault Secures Financing and Issues Warrants for Sosa Project
data.description:
Energy Vault Holdings ( (NRGV) ) just unveiled an update.

On November 16, 2026, certain Energy Vault subsidiaries entered financing agreements for the approximately 150 MW / 300 MWh Sosa battery energy storage project in Madison County, Texas. The facilities comprised a $78.0 million preferred equity bridge loan and an $8.7 million letter of credit facility; on November 19, 2026, the bridge facility was funded and the Company drew $27.2 million.

The agreements provided for a third-party investor’s $79.6 million investment in Sosa Partnership, subject to funding conditions and installments. Also on November 19, 2026, OIC funded approximately $38.3 million to Asset Vault, and the Company issued OIC warrants to buy up to 6,089,009 common shares at $4.080375 each.

data.title: iBio Receives Nasdaq Bid Price Compliance Deficiency Notice
data.description:
The latest update is out from Ibio ( (IBIO) ).

On November 19, 2026, iBio, Inc. received Nasdaq notice that its common stock had failed to maintain the $1 minimum closing bid price during the 30-business-day period from October 8 through November 18. The notice did not immediately affect the stock’s Nasdaq Capital Market listing; iBio had until May 18, 2027, to regain compliance, with possible additional time subject to Nasdaq requirements, while Nasdaq said the stock could become subject to delisting if the deficiency was not cured and iBio was not eligible for additional time.

data.title: Southwest Gas Amends Bylaws and Executive Benefit Plans
data.description:
Southwest Gas ( (SWX) ) has shared an update.

On November 17, 2026, the boards of Southwest Gas Holdings, Inc. and Southwest Gas Corporation approved changes to Southwest Gas’ deferred compensation and nonqualified retirement plans. The Executive Deferral Plan was amended to freeze new contributions effective February 28, 2027, change the interest rate on deferred amounts and clarify administrative provisions, while a new Deferred Compensation Plan was adopted with administrative and record-keeping benefits and substantially similar participant benefits, but a different rate for termination-related distributions.

Also on November 17, 2026, the Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan was amended to allow officers hired on or after January 1, 2022, to participate, with retirement eligibility at age 55 after 10 years of service and related disability and death benefits. Retirement and disability benefits start at 30% of average earnings and can rise by 2% for each additional full service year to 40%, while eligible surviving spouses may receive 50% of the retirement benefit; specified pension and disability-related benefits reduce amounts payable.

The Company also adopted amended and restated bylaws on November 17, 2026, effective immediately, revising stockholder meeting procedures to reflect Delaware law changes and expanding advance-notice requirements for nominations and other proposals to reflect the Securities and Exchange Commission’s universal proxy rules. The bylaws provide for uncertificated, book-entry shares unless the Board authorizes certificates, while existing certificated shares remain certificated until surrendered.

data.title: PMV Pharmaceuticals Presents Updated PYNNACLE Trial Data
data.description:
PMV Pharmaceuticals ( (PMVP) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On November 20, 2026, PMV Pharmaceuticals reported updated data from the pivotal Phase 2 portion of the PYNNACLE trial, which evaluated rezatapopt monotherapy in patients with TP53 Y220C-mutated advanced solid tumors. The data were presented that day as a late-breaking oral presentation at ENA 2026 in Barcelona, Spain.

In 65 platinum-resistant or refractory ovarian cancer patients who had received prior standard care, investigator-assessed overall response rate was 48%, median duration of response was 10.4 months and disease control rate was 83%. Among 168 evaluable patients across all cohorts, overall response rate was 36% and median duration of response was 8.1 months; responses were observed across eight tumor types, while treatment-related adverse events were mostly Grade 1 or 2 and 11 patients discontinued treatment because of them.

data.title: Cracker Barrel Shareholders Elect Directors, Approve Compensation and Auditor
data.description:
Cracker Barrel ( (CBRL) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On November 19, 2026, Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. held its annual shareholder meeting, where nine director nominees were elected. Shareholders also approved, on an advisory basis, executive compensation and ratified Deloitte & Touche LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for the company’s 2027 fiscal year.

The shareholder proposal requiring approval before issuing “blank check” preferred stock, subject to limited exceptions, was not approved. Corporate Election Services certified the results, with 18,874,410 of 22,352,430 shares outstanding and entitled to vote present in person or represented by proxy.
